findings.description: An AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables. They are exposed in the repository, in Terraform state, and to any principal with lambda:GetFunction/GetFunctionConfiguration, providing long-lived credentials to an attacker.

No kms_key_arn is set, so the environment variables holding these secrets are protected only by the default AWS-managed key; anyone with lambda:GetFunction can read them in cleartext without needing a distinct KMS grant. A customer-managed CMK with a restricted key policy would add an access-control boundary around the secrets.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which is past end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime unpatched.

The function has no vpc_config, so it executes outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet egress and no security group boundary. Combined with the embedded static credentials, this eases exfiltration if the function code is compromised.

findings.issue_category: missing confused-deputy protection in trust policy
findings.description: The assume-role policy allows lambda.amazonaws.com to assume the role with no aws:SourceAccount or aws:SourceArn condition, so any Lambda function in any account that the service principal can act for is not constrained by the trust relationship. Adding source-account/source-ARN conditions scopes the trust to this account's functions.
